National Weather Service Burlington VT
739 AM EDT Sun Sep 27 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 237 AM EDT Sunday...

No significant changes have been made to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 237 AM EDT Sunday...

1. A Nor'easter will continue to bring rounds of showers to the 
region through Monday, with breezy winds gradually diminishing 
through the day today.  

2. Above normal temperatures Wednesday and Thursday. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 237 AM EDT Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: The Nor'easter to our south continues to be the focus of 
the forecast as we remain on the periphery of the system. Throughout 
the day today, several rounds of showers are expected to move 
through, with more measurable precipitation in comparison to 
yesterday. Total rainfall amounts associated with this system will 
vary greatly depending on location, with 1 to 1.5 inches expected 
across southern Vermont by Monday afternoon while northern New York 
will likely only see a few hundredths in the same time period. Given 
the long duration of this event, rain will be largely beneficial 
with no hydrological concerns. Shower activity will gradually taper 
off Monday as the low shifts eastward, with drier weather 
anticipated for Tuesday and Wednesday. In addition to the 
precipitation, breezy winds will continue across the region this 
morning given the strong pressure gradient, although the winds look 
to gradually diminish throughout the day as the pressure gradient 
weakens with winds trending light by Monday night. Gusts this 
afternoon looks to generally be in the 15 to 25 mph range, with the 
greatest concern across mountain summits. Temperatures will be on 
the cooler side as well, especially for Sunday and Monday with 
clouds and periods of showers expected, especially across southern 
and eastern Vermont.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A narrow 700-500mb ridge axis brings a tranquil start to 
the extended forecast period Tuesday night and Wednesday with light 
winds and slightly above normal temperatures. Any lingering low
clouds should dissipate with increased subsidence. Highs on 
Wednesday and Thursday should reach the low-mid 70s in most 
valley locations. A modest cold front will bring a period of 
mainly light rain showers Thursday night into Friday morning. 
Max PoPs for this system currently around 50 percent, and 
rainfall amounts are generally expected to remain below 0.25". 
Gusty NW winds following frontal passage ushers in cool and dry 
conditions later Friday and into Saturday. With 850mb 
temperatures near 0C Saturday afternoon, daytime highs will be 
significantly cooler to start the weekend, with highs generally 
in the 50s.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Through 12Z Monday...The northern fringe of the Nor'easter
centered south of Long Island early this AM will bring 
scattered rain showers and periods of LLWS to the North Country
TAF sites today, with the greatest impacts at our southern and 
eastern TAF sites including BTV/RUT/MPV/EFK. While ceilings and
vsby will mostly remain MVFR or better, increasing chances for 
showers begin around 11-12Z at RUT/MPV and by 13Z at EFK/BTV.
Best chances for occasional MVFR conditions and HIR TRRN OBSCD 
during the daylight hours today will be at RUT and MPV, and 
mainly due to ceilings. 

Winds will generally be N to NE, with gusts 20-25kt becoming 
increasingly common during the daylight hours. During periods in
which stronger wind gusts don't reach the surface, it appears 
that pockets of LLWS will be possible. MSS should be northwest 
of most of the shower and LLWS activity and is expected to 
remain VFR through the TAF period. 

Outlook...

Monday: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Monday Night: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Tuesday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Thursday: VFR. NO SIG WX.

&&

.MARINE...
As of 237 AM EDT Sunday...

The Lake Wind Advisory remains in effect for the southern waters and 
broad waters of Lake Champlain this morning. Sustained north winds 
of 15 to 25 knots and gusts of 30 knots will remain possible
throughout the morning. Winds will continue to diminish 
through the day today, becoming around 10 knots by the evening.
Waves are generally 2-5 feet, subsiding to 1-3 feet as the day 
progresses.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
